fullPassage: Despite the cultural trope depicting emotions as the opposite of rational thought, cognition — what we commonly refer to as thinking — is actually a key building block of emotion. How we think about our circumstances shapes the emotions we experience; then those emotions echo back to influence how we think. For instance, if you walk into a test thinking you are bad at taking tests, your anxiety will be increased. Then you don't feel good about your performance on the test, and that becomes evidence for continuing to think that you're bad at test taking. This bi-directionality of cognition and emotion allows us to adjust difficult emotions by changing the way we think. By thinking differently — I get nervous sometimes, but I'm still a good test taker, or that nervous feeling is just excitement and anticipation, it means I'm ready — you can work those pathways to your advantage.

❌③ a barrier to emotional control(감정 조절의 장애물): 글은 오히려 생각을 바꿔 감정을 조절할 수 있다고 하므로 반대예요.

❌④ an echo of our past memories(과거 기억의 메아리): echo는 뒤 문장의 표현을 엉뚱하게 끌어온 오답이에요.

questions.passage: Despite the cultural trope depicting emotions as the opposite of rational thought, cognition — what we commonly refer to as thinking — is actually a key building block of emotion. How we think about our circumstances shapes the emotions we experience; then those emotions echo back to influence how we think. For instance, if you walk into a test thinking you are bad at taking tests, your anxiety will be increased. Then you don't feel good about your performance on the test, and that becomes evidence for continuing to think that you're bad at test taking. This bi-directionality of cognition and emotion allows us to adjust difficult emotions by changing the way we think. By thinking differently — I get nervous sometimes, but I'm still a good test taker, or that nervous feeling is just excitement and anticipation, it means I'm ready — you can work those pathways to your advantage.

det.korean: 'A가 ~할 수 있게 해 주다'는 allow + 목적어 + to부정사 구조예요. 주어 This bi-directionality(단수)에 맞춰 allows, 목적어 us, 목적격보어 to adjust difficult emotions로 이어요.
det.analysis:
① '~할 수 있게 해 주다' = allow + 목적어 + to부정사. 주어 This bi-directionality가 단수라 allows.

② 목적어 '우리가' = us (allow의 목적어라 목적격).

③ 목적격보어 '힘든 감정을 조절하다' = to adjust difficult emotions (to부정사 + 형용사 difficult + 명사 emotions).

➡ 순서대로 이으면 allows / us / to / adjust / difficult / emotions (총 6단어).
det.tip: allow + O + to-V = O가 ~할 수 있게 해 주다

questions.wa: allows us to adjust difficult emotions
accept: allows us to adjust difficult emotions

questions.passage: Despite the cultural trope depicting emotions as the opposite of rational thought, cognition — what we commonly refer to as thinking — is actually a key building block of emotion. How we think about our circumstances shapes the emotions we experience; then those emotions echo back to influence how we think. For instance, if you walk into a test thinking you are bad at taking tests, your anxiety will be increased. Then you don't feel good about your performance on the test, and that becomes evidence for continuing to think that you're bad at test taking. This bi-directionality of cognition and emotion allows us to adjust difficult emotions by changing the way we think. By thinking differently — I get nervous sometimes, but I'm still a good test taker, or __________, it means I'm ready — you can work those pathways to your advantage.
questions.stem:
다음 우리말에 맞도록 주어진 단어를 올바른 순서로 배열하시오.
"그 긴장되는 느낌은 그저 설렘과 기대일 뿐이다"

[ and / anticipation / excitement / feeling / is / just / nervous / that ] (8단어) (영어로)

det.korean: 주어 '그 긴장되는 느낌' = that nervous feeling, 동사 is, 보어 '그저 설렘과 기대' = just excitement and anticipation 순서로 배열해요.
det.analysis:
① 주어 '그 긴장되는 느낌' = that nervous feeling (지시형용사 that + 형용사 nervous + 명사 feeling).

② 동사 '~이다' = is (주어 feeling이 단수).

③ 보어 '그저 설렘과 기대' = just excitement and anticipation (부사 just + 명사 excitement + and + 명사 anticipation).

➡ 순서대로 이으면 that / nervous / feeling / is / just / excitement / and / anticipation (총 8단어).
det.tip: that(지시형용사) + 형용사 + 명사 → that nervous feeling

questions.wa: that nervous feeling is just excitement and anticipation
accept: that nervous feeling is just excitement and anticipation

How we think about our circumstances shapes the emotions we experience; then those emotions echo back to influence how we think. For instance, if you walk into a test thinking you are bad at taking tests, your anxiety will be increased. Then you don't feel good about your performance on the test, and that __________ that you're bad at test taking. By thinking differently — I get nervous sometimes, but I'm still a good test taker, or that nervous feeling is just excitement and anticipation, it means I'm ready — you can work those pathways to your advantage.
questions.stem:
다음 우리말 뜻에 맞도록 주어진 단어를 모두 배열하여 빈칸을 완성하시오.

"~라고 계속 생각하게 하는 근거가 된다" (6단어) (영어로) [조건] (1) becomes, continuing, evidence, for, think, to 를 모두 사용 (2) 정확히 6단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: '~의 근거가 되다' = becomes evidence for ~. 전치사 for 뒤에는 동명사 continuing이 오고, continue는 to부정사를 목적어로 취해 continuing to think로 이어요.
det.analysis:
① '근거가 된다' = becomes evidence (주어 that이 단수라 becomes).

② '~하는 것에 대한' = 전치사 for + 동명사 → for continuing (전치사 뒤는 동명사).

③ '계속 생각하다' = continue to think → 동명사형 continuing to think (continue + to부정사).

➡ 순서대로 이으면 becomes / evidence / for / continuing / to / think (총 6단어).
det.tip: 전치사 for + 동명사(continuing) + to부정사(to think)

questions.wa: becomes evidence for continuing to think
accept: becomes evidence for continuing to think
